- **Ship class & type** – HMS Sharpshooter was a **Halcyon‑class minesweeper** of the Royal Navy.  
- **Construction** – Built at **Devonport Dockyard**; **completed** in **1937**.  
- **Dimensions & performance** –  
  - Displacement: **1 310 t** (full load)  
  - Length: **74.75 m**  
  - Speed: **17 kn**  
  - Complement: **80** sailors/officers.  
- **Armament** – Two **QF 4 in Mk V (L/45 102 mm)** guns, single mounts; four **QF 0.5 in Mk III (12.7 mm) Vickers** machine‑guns, quad mount.  
- **Operational history** –  
  - Served throughout **World II** in both its designed minesweeping role and as a convoy escort, including several **Arctic convoys**.  
  - On **24 March 1942** it successfully sank the German submarine **U‑655** while escorting convoy **QP 9**. The sinking was achieved by a direct hit that rammed the submarine, resulting in its loss. The ship’s bow was heavily damaged; repairs lasted **through June 1942**.  
  - After World II ended, in **May 1945** it was **converted to a survey ship** (armament removed). Served in this role until placed in reserve in **1961**; removed from the disposal list in **1965** and later sold for scrapping.  
- **Commanding officer at sinking** – **Lt‑Cdr. David Lampen** (referred to on the page as “captain”) was commanding HMS Sharpshooter during the *U‑655* incident. The page notes he called “Emergency full ahead” and “Stand by to ram” during the engagement.  
- **Other personnel** – The page does **not** list any additional commanding officers or their honours.
